surface_forms: Son Excellence le duc de Sidonia

appraisal_events.evidence: l'intarissable jacassement de M. de Charlus... ils avaient pris la détermination... de parler chacun sans s'occuper de ce que dirait l'autre... les tonnerres qu'il brandissait... commençaient à passer, selon beaucoup de gens... pour des tonnerres en carton
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator portrays Charlus as a comic, self-absorbed monologist locked in parallel non-listening with a rival talker, and states plainly that many now see his once-feared threats as empty bluster, even if novices still find him formidable.

appraisal_events.evidence: un homme assez vulgaire... jamais on n'avait vu... un personnage de sa sorte [chez la princesse]... « Madame votre grand'mère est bien morte, n'est-ce pas ? » me dit-il d'une voix où une quasi-certitude calmait une légère appréhension... mon pronostic avait été tout à fait sombre, je me souviens très bien
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator frames the professor as a vulgar outsider admitted only as a favor, whose tactless question about the grandmother's death — asked mainly to protect his own diagnostic record — exposes him as callous and socially graceless.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator's mocking description of his endless, unlistening chatter locally lowers him.
The passage explicitly states that many people now regard his threats and authority as spent, cardboard thunder, even though novices may still be overawed.
He is directly called vulgar and shown to be tactless and self-interested when tactlessly confirming the grandmother's death only to protect his diagnostic reputation.
